title: Satoshi Tajiri: The Creator of Pokémon
summary: Satoshi Tajiri turned his childhood love of collecting insects into Pokémon, a worldwide phenomenon about catching and trading creatures.
imageAlt: Stylized illustration of Satoshi Tajiri with a bug net and a classic handheld game console.
author: Jacob Sutanto
body: Long before he created Pokémon, Satoshi Tajiri was a boy who loved exploring the fields and forests of rural Tokyo, Japan. He spent his days searching for insects, which he would catch, study, and trade with his friends. His collection grew so large that his friends nicknamed him "Dr. Bug." He loved the thrill of finding a rare beetle. But as he grew up, the fields and ponds he loved were replaced by buildings and parking lots. He worried that future kids wouldn't get to experience the joy of discovering and collecting creatures.

As a teenager, Satoshi's passion shifted from bugs to arcade games. He spent hours at the local arcade, mastering games and learning their secrets. He wanted to share his knowledge with others, so he started a handmade magazine called *Game Freak*. He and his friend, Ken Sugimori, who drew the art, would write, print, and staple the magazines themselves. *Game Freak* became popular with other gamers who wanted to learn tips and tricks.

One day, Satoshi saw two people playing on their Nintendo Game Boys, connected by a Link Cable. An idea sparked in his mind. He imagined insects crawling across the cable, from one Game Boy to the other. This made him think of his childhood bug-collecting days. What if he could create a game where players could catch, train, and trade creatures just like he did with his insects? He wanted to give all kids the same feeling of discovery he had.

Satoshi turned his magazine, *Game Freak*, into a video game company. He and his team spent six long years working on his idea. It was a difficult process, and they almost ran out of money. But Satoshi believed in his dream. He presented his idea to Nintendo, who saw the magic in catching and trading monsters.

Finally, in 1996, *Pokémon Red* and *Pokémon Green* were released in Japan. The games were a huge success! Players loved exploring the world, catching all 151 original Pokémon, and trading with friends to complete their Pokédex. The game fulfilled Satoshi's dream of letting everyone experience the joy of collecting.

Satoshi Tajiri's story shows how a childhood passion can turn into a creative idea that connects people all over the world. His love for bug collecting became a game that has been enjoyed by millions for decades, reminding us all to "Gotta Catch 'Em All!"
